SAS LOGSDF(distribution, quantile <, parameters>)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_logsdf.Rd

Logarithm of the survival function. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

dist

Character name of the distribution, not case sensitive: 'NORMAL' (or 'GAUSS'), 'T', 'CHISQ', 'F', 'BINOMIAL', 'POISSON', 'UNIFORM', 'EXPONENTIAL', 'BETA', 'GAMMA' or 'LOGNORMAL'.

x

Numeric value at which the function is evaluated (a count for discrete distributions). A missing value gives a missing result.

...

Distribution parameters in the order SAS 9.4 defines: NORMAL location and scale (default 0, 1); T df <, nc>; CHISQ df <, nc>; F ndf, ddf <, nc>; BINOMIAL p, n; POISSON mean; UNIFORM left, right (default 0, 1); EXPONENTIAL scale (default 1); BETA a, b; GAMMA shape <, scale>; LOGNORMAL location, scale (default 0, 1).

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Arguments and parameterisation are those of the SAS function (order of arguments, noncentrality), not those of R's d/p/q/r functions.

See also

Other probability functions: sas_f_cdf(), sas_f_cinv(), sas_f_finv(), sas_f_logcdf(), sas_f_logpdf(), sas_f_pdf(), sas_f_poisson(), sas_f_probbnml(), sas_f_probchi(), sas_f_probf(), sas_f_probit(), sas_f_probnorm(), sas_f_probt(), sas_f_quantile(), sas_f_sdf(), sas_f_tinv()

Examples

# LOGSDF: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# LOGSDF is approximate: in strict mode (the default) a direct call stops; these calls
# run with options(sasonr.strict = FALSE) and a warning of class sasonr_strict_warning.
old <- options(sasonr.strict = FALSE)

# The log of the normal survival function P(X > 0) is log(0.5).
sas_f_logsdf("NORMAL", 0)  # logsdf('NORMAL', 0) = -0.693147180559945
#> Warning: sasonr: function LOGSDF is approximate
#> This warning is displayed once per session.
#> [1] -0.6931472

# Far in the upper tail LOGSDF stays accurate although P(X > 10) is only about
# 7.6E-24.
sas_f_logsdf("NORMAL", 10)  # logsdf('NORMAL', 10) = -53.2312851505125
#> [1] -53.23129

# A missing quantile gives a missing result.
sas_f_logsdf("NORMAL", NA_real_)  # logsdf('NORMAL', .) = .
#> [1] NA

options(old)
